content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (fallback cure), confidence 0.85.**

What I found across all responsive locations:

- **§ 13.5 (p0208)** expressly deems *two* Customer-payable amounts "liquidated damages and not a penalty."
- **§ 11.1 (p0187)** — Termination for Convenience Fee: REDACTED % of Estimated Remaining Value, outside the § 13.4 cap.
- **§ 11.2(A) (p0189)** — Termination for Cause Fee: same base, triggered by Customer's Event of Default or defective notice, also outside the § 13.4 cap.
- **§ 1(N) (p0039)** — "Estimated Remaining Value" is measured on months remaining to end of Term, i.e. remaining contract value (walk-away territory).
- Checked and left alone: § 11.2(B) (no fee on M&I default — benefits us), § 9.2(D) service credits to us (REDACTED, noted), § 8.13 collection fees/Damages and default repricing (pricing/indemnity mechanics, not liquidated amounts, and now covered by the "sole liquidated amount" sentence).

Cure (three surgical replaces, fallback level): cap the fee at three months' average Fees; substitute that same early-termination fee for the Cause Fee, retiring the defined term so no dangling reference survives in § 11.2(A) or § 13.5; and confirm it is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer. Payment mechanics and the unrelated Expenses sentence are preserved verbatim, and quantum is argued only here rather than duplicated under the convenience-termination rule.
